title: Pardons Amy Ralston Povah
description_medium: President Donald Trump granted Amy Ralston Povah a full pardon on January 13, 2021. A federal court had sentenced her in 1992 to 292 months for drug conspiracy and money-laundering offenses; President Bill Clinton commuted that prison term to time served in 2000. Trump’s pardon was a separate act. Povah founded the CAN-DO Foundation, a clemency advocacy group.
description_long: President Donald Trump’s January 13, 2021 clemency announcement included a full pardon for Amy Ralston Povah. Her federal case began with a 1992 sentence of 292 months in prison for drug conspiracy and money-laundering offenses. President Bill Clinton commuted that prison sentence to time served in 2000, more than two decades before Trump’s pardon. The warrant records both the original sentence and the earlier commutation, while the DOJ list confirms the later grant. Povah founded the CAN-DO Foundation, which advocates for clemency and criminal-justice reform. The records establish the pardon and her prior sentence history; they do not state a recipient-specific reason for Trump’s decision. The January 2021 event was therefore a pardon following an earlier commutation, not an immediate release from a sentence she was then serving. Her organizing work explains her public association with clemency advocacy, but the record does not say that advocacy prompted the presidential decision.
rationale: The warrant and DOJ list confirm pardon and prior commutation; they do not provide Trump’s recipient-specific rationale.

title: Pardons Faustino Bernadett
description_medium: President Donald Trump granted Dr. Faustino Bernadett a full pardon in January 2021, before he was due to report to prison. Bernadett, former owner of Pacific Hospital in Long Beach, was sentenced to 15 months for misprision of a felony tied to a health-care kickback scheme. The court also imposed a $60,000 fine and supervised release.
description_long: Dr. Faustino Bernadett, a physician and former Pacific Hospital owner, received a full pardon from President Donald Trump in January 2021, before his scheduled surrender to prison. Bernadett had been sentenced to 15 months after pleading guilty to misprision of a felony. The Justice Department described the underlying health-care fraud as a kickback scheme in which doctors, chiropractors and marketers received payments for referring patients to Pacific Hospital for spinal surgeries and other services, many billed to California workers’ compensation insurers. The court also imposed a $60,000 fine and one year of supervised release. The White House said Bernadett had not initiated the kickback scheme and cited his charitable work. The clemency record confirms that the pardon came before the custodial sentence began. The case grew out of a broad kickback arrangement tied to patient referrals, rather than a standalone tax offense; the DOJ account describes payments and referral relationships while the White House cited Bernadett’s charitable work.
rationale: DOJ and White House accounts provide the case context and publicly stated support for clemency.

title: Pardons Tommaso Buti in Unresolved Federal Case
description_medium: President Donald Trump pardoned Italian businessman Tommaso Buti on January 19, 2021. DOJ lists an indictment in the Southern District of New York for conspiracy and fraud-related charges, with no resolution or sentence recorded. Buti was known for co-founding Fashion Cafe, a New York restaurant chain promoted with Claudia Schiffer, Naomi Campbell and Elle Macpherson.
description_long: President Donald Trump pardoned Tommaso Buti on January 19, 2021. The Justice Department’s clemency list describes Buti as indicted in the Southern District of New York, with no further resolution recorded and no sentence listed. The charges included conspiracy to defraud the United States, wire fraud and money laundering. Buti was known in the 1990s for co-founding Fashion Cafe, a New York restaurant chain promoted with models Claudia Schiffer, Naomi Campbell and Elle Macpherson. Contemporary reporting connected the federal investigation to the restaurant chain’s collapse and noted that it had not resulted in a conviction. The listed charges were allegations rather than findings of guilt. The official list confirms the pardon but does not explain why Trump selected Buti or provide an individual warrant in the cited record. Fashion Cafe’s celebrity-backed branding made it a conspicuous New York venture, but the legal entry concerns allegations tied to its business collapse and leaves their adjudication unresolved.

corrected_wording.rationale: The Justice Department list describes an unresolved indictment, not a conviction.

title: Pardons George Gilmore
description_medium: President Donald Trump granted George Gilmore a full pardon on January 19, 2021. Gilmore, an Ocean County, New Jersey attorney and Republican political leader, was convicted of failing to pay payroll taxes withheld from employees and making a false statement on a bank-loan application. He was sentenced to one year and one day in prison in 2020.
description_long: President Donald Trump granted George Gilmore a full pardon on January 19, 2021. Gilmore, an Ocean County, New Jersey attorney and longtime Republican political leader, had been convicted of failing to pay payroll taxes withheld from law-firm employees and making a false statement on a bank-loan application. A jury acquitted him of two tax-return counts and could not reach a verdict on a separate income-tax-evasion count. In January 2020 he received a sentence of one year and one day in prison, but remained free on bail when Trump pardoned him. Gilmore had resigned as Ocean County Republican chairman after his conviction. The White House announcement listed supporters of his pardon application and described his community service. These facts document the case and public support; they do not independently establish an improper exchange. His pardon followed his conviction while the sentence was pending, and the clemency action did not erase the separate jury outcomes.
rationale: DOJ and White House records establish the mixed verdict, sentence, timing and supporters, without proving an improper exchange.
